newsitem.title: USA: US corp bonds higher at noon,Grand Casino volatile.
newsitem.headline: US corp bonds higher at noon,Grand Casino volatile.

text.p: U.S. high-grade corporate bonds dipped after an unexpected rise in August consumer confidence but remained in positive territory at noon, while junk-rated Grand Casinos Inc notes rose in volatile trade, dealers said.

Sent into a spin on news of a surprisingly large charge against future earnings, Grand Casinos' 10-1/8 percent first mortgage notes were last quoted up 1/4 at 97-1/2, but traded in a 96-1/2 to 97-1/2 range.
"Grands are trading all over the place," one dealer said.
Grand said on Tuesday it expects to record a non-cash charge of $0.55 to $0.60 in the second half of fiscal 1996 as a result of operating losses at Stratosphere Corp.
Grand said the charge is about $0.50 per share higher than originally estimated. Grand Casinos owns about 42 percent of Stratosphere.
Stratosphere's 14-1/4 percent first mortgage notes were quoted unchanged at 82-1/2 bid, 84-1/4 offer but no trades had been seen.
In other gaming debt, Trump Atlantic City 11-1/4 percent first mortgage notes were quoted off at 94-3/4 bid, 95 offer.
Overall, the high-yield market was mostly unchanged in thin trade.
Slow trade also plagued the investment-grade arena with Treasuries setting the tone and spreads not budging, dealers said.

Market attention was focused on the Treasury's monthly two-year note auction. The Department will sell $18.75 billion in two-year notes with bidding closing at 1300 EDT/1700 GMT. Results are expected at 1345 EDT/1745 GMT.
The benchmark 30-year long bond was up 13/32 at 97-09/32 to yield 6.97 percent at 1230 GMT/1630 GMT.
Two pending bank new issues have punctuated a slow week in the primary market, syndicate sources said.
Swiss Bank Corp is expected to tap the market with a $400 million two-part AA2/AA rated subordinated notes via Swiss Bank. Both tranches are noncallable, sources said.

The deal consist of a 10-year maturity with price talk seen at 50 basis points over U.S. Treasuries. The second maturity consist of a 30-year issue with price talk seen in the 70 basis points range, sources added.

In addition, Key Bank-NY is expected to price $165 million in A1/A-minus rated subordinated notes due 2008 via Salomon Brothers. Price talk on the issue is in the mid-70 basis points range, dealers said.
